## Introduction

This document showcases interactive Shiny components running entirely in the browser via shinylive (webR). No server required!

## Species Selector

Select a species to see information about it:

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 350

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput("species", "Select Species:",
              choices = c("Species A", "Species B", "Species C")),
  hr(),
  h4(textOutput("species_info")),
  tableOutput("species_table")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  species_data <- data.frame(
    species = c("Species A", "Species B", "Species C"),
    lat = c(37.7749, 40.7128, 34.0522),
    lon = c(-122.4194, -74.0060, -118.2437),
    count = c(50, 30, 40),
    region = c("West Coast", "East Coast", "West Coast")
  )

  output$species_info <- renderText({
    paste("Showing data for:", input$species)
  })

  output$species_table <- renderTable({
    species_data[species_data$species == input$species, ]
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

## Historical Data Explorer

Use the slider to select a year and see how observations change:

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 350

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  sliderInput("year", "Select Year:", min = 2020, max = 2023, value = 2023, step = 1),
  hr(),
  h4(textOutput("year_summary")),
  plotOutput("year_plot", height = "200px")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  yearly_data <- data.frame(
    year = rep(2020:2023, each = 3),
    species = rep(c("Species A", "Species B", "Species C"), 4),
    count = c(40, 25, 35, 45, 28, 38, 48, 32, 42, 50, 30, 40)
  )

  output$year_summary <- renderText({
    yr_data <- yearly_data[yearly_data$year == input$year, ]
    paste("In", input$year, "we observed", sum(yr_data$count),
          "total occurrences across all species.")
  })

  output$year_plot <- renderPlot({
    yr_data <- yearly_data[yearly_data$year == input$year, ]
    barplot(yr_data$count, names.arg = yr_data$species,
            col = c("#2196F3", "#4CAF50", "#FF9800"),
            main = paste("Species Counts in", input$year),
            ylab = "Count", ylim = c(0, 60))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

## Conclusion

These interactive components demonstrate Shiny apps running directly in your browser using shinylive and webR — no R server needed.
